body: Westbrook just called - Anna left her history project on the kitchen counter. Can you run it over before 10? I'm stuck in a client meeting til noon.
I'm 40 minutes into my focus block but yes, I'll go. Tell them 9:45. This is the second time this month.
I know, I know. Also Karen texted, wants to do lunch Thursday in Thornfield. You free?
Thursday works after 1. Tell her the new place on Marlowe St, not the faculty club. I'm done running into colleagues on my off hours.
Just dropped you and realized I forgot to mention - Dad's doing pickup today. I have a 4pm lab meeting and I can't leave the sequence analysis mid-run. Text him directly if anything comes up.
ok but can u PLEASE tell him not to be late again 😭 also can i go to Maya's after school?
I'll remind him. Maya's is fine but be home by 7, Karen's coming over and I'll need an extra set of hands setting up.
omg Karen?? yes I'll definitely be home, she always brings those cookies 😭 ok see you at 7

Anna's science fair is next Thursday at Westbrook Academy. She built an age-appropriate CRISPR model for it. Thought you'd want to know, given it's technically your granddaughter doing your daughter's job.
Ha! I'll be there. Should I drive up to Thornfield Wednesday night or Thursday morning? Is Steve around?
Thursday morning is fine, presentation's at 10. Steve's making dinner after so plan to stay - Anna's been asking when you're visiting anyway.
Perfect. Tell her grandfather expects a full debrief on the methodology. Proud of her 🧬
Did Anna's last day at Westbrook go alright? She texted me three crying emojis and I couldn't tell if that was good crying or bad crying 😅
Situational crying, said goodbye to her teacher, recovered in under five minutes, then immediately lobbied for a hamster. Steve is already wavering, which I am monitoring closely.
Oh he'll cave, you know he will lol. Are you done with that grant yet or are you still barricading yourself in your office every morning before Anna's even awake?
Draft due Friday. The morning blocks are holding but barely. Should be an actual human being again by the weekend.
Did Anna's Westbrook end-of-year thing happen yet? Was hoping to catch it if there's still something coming up 😬
It was Thursday. She played two pieces in the string ensemble. Held her own against the 8th graders. Steve cried, obviously.
OF COURSE he did 😂 wish I'd been there. Is she home all summer or does she have camp?
Two weeks of her underfoot, then three weeks at science camp in Vermont. My deep focus blocks are already under negotiation.
Anna got 2nd place at the Westbrook science fair today. She's devastated. Steve bought a cake that says 'You Tried' on it and I have told him that is not helping.
LMAO Steve 😭 is she actually upset or is this a 20-minute thing
She cried through dinner and then asked me to teach her proteomics so she can 'destroy everyone next year.' I suggested she start with the cell cycle.
honestly that's the most you response possible. she is going to be you in 20 years, Thornfield's scariest computational biologist 😂
Pipeline finished overnight - alignment rates on the new HeLa batch are worse than March, ~62% vs 78%. Before we flag it with the consortium, did you adjust the trimming params last week?
Oh, yes, I bumped quality cutoff to Q30 for the resubmission. Almost certainly explains it. Want me to rerun with Q20 and diff the outputs?
Yes, pull the flagged reads too. I've got Anna's pickup at 3 so I'm out of my focus block after that. I can review whatever you push tonight.
Done by 2 easily. I'll commit to the shared repo and drop you the run log. 🧬

The DESeq2 run finished overnight - cluster 4 is showing strong upregulation in all three replicates but only in the Thornfield cohort samples. Might be a batch effect or something real. Worth a look before I push to the manuscript?
Don't push anything yet. Check the PCA first, if the Thornfield samples are separating on PC2 we have a confound, not a finding. Send me the variance-stabilized counts when you have them.
PCA incoming. Also the Haverstone core is asking about sequencing order metadata, apparently it wasn't in the submission? I can chase that down if you're in your morning block.
Yes, handle it. Metadata should be in the shared drive under /raw/batch_info. If it's not there email Priya at the core directly. Don't let it stall the resubmission.
Hey Dorothy - DE pipeline for the Thornfield cohort just finished. FDR cutoffs are behaving strangely in the 14q22 window specifically. Worth a look before the 2pm slot?
In my focus block until noon, nothing scheduled before then. Flag the 14q22 loci and I'll pull the QC plots myself. Did you check whether batch correction ran cleanly?
Batch looks fine. Think it's the housekeeping gene normalization. Three references overlap that window and they're pulling the thresholds. Might need GENCODE v45.
Swap the annotation and rerun that region only. We'll go through it at 2. Archive the original run - don't overwrite it.

Wei, your batch correction script is collapsing the Thornfield cohort samples with the controls again. Third time this month. Fix the sample ID filter before I look at the updated PCA tomorrow morning.
Oh no, I thought I caught that. Is it the metadata CSV or the script itself?
Script. The regex isn't anchoring on cohort prefix. Check lines 47-52. I need the corrected output before 8am; Anna's school run isn't movable and I want to review before I leave.
On it right now, really sorry. I'll push the fix to the repo by 7:30 so you have time to check it.
Dorothy - Anna absolutely nailed the fouetté sequence in Thursday's class. She's been so consistent lately. Whatever you two are doing at home, keep it up 🩰
That's good to hear. She's been drilling it in the kitchen every morning before we leave for Westbrook, Steve nearly lost a coffee mug on Tuesday.
Ha! Worth the sacrifice. I'd like to move her to the intermediate group in September if she keeps this up. Wanted to flag it before summer break starts.
Noted, she'll be pleased. Send the fall schedule when you have it and I'll work it around my research blocks. Thursdays are usually manageable.
Dorothy - following up on Anna's throat culture from yesterday. Results just came back negative for strep, so likely viral. Keep her home from Westbrook one more day and push fluids.
Good to know, I assumed viral given the absence of exudate, but wanted confirmation before sending her back. She's been afebrile since this morning, so I'll reassess tomorrow.
Exactly right. If fever returns or she's not eating by Thursday, bring her in. Otherwise you're fine. Hope your research block isn't too disrupted!
It's survivable. Computational biology waits, Anna doesn't. Thanks, Anita.
Lisa. Any chance you have a slot Thursday after 3? Anna has her spring recital at Westbrook Friday morning and I'd rather not stack appointments that week.
Thursday at 3:30 is open! I can move you from your usual Tuesday. Full hour?
3:30 works. Full hour, yes - I've been back at the standing desk configuration Steve keeps insisting I have no problem with.
Ha. Noted. See you Thursday 👍
RNA-seq results just dropped into the shared drive, prelim QC looks clean, >90% mapping across all 12 samples. Want me to flag anything before your focus block kicks in?
Don't flag, just run FastQC on the batch 2 outlier and leave the summary in the usual folder. I'll pull it up after I drop Anna at Westbrook.
On it. Also the Illumina rep wants to reschedule the NovaSeq demo. Proposing Thursday 10am. Doesn't that conflict with your Haverstone seminar slot?
It does. Tuesday afternoon works if they can accommodate it. If not, they're welcome to demo to someone with a more flexible calendar.
Priya - the STAR alignment output from last night's run, did you check the mapping rates for samples 7 and 12? They looked low when I skimmed the log this morning before dropping Anna off.
Yes! Both under 65%, I think it's the rRNA contamination we flagged last month. Rerunning with the updated blacklist now, should have cleaner output by noon.
Good. Document it in the methods log either way. Karen Sutherland's lab is using the same library prep kit and if it's a batch issue they'll need to know.
Will do. Should I email Dr. Sutherland directly or route it through you first?
Daniel - the RNA-seq alignment output from Friday's run has ~22% unmapped reads in the cortex samples. That's well above threshold. Check the trimming parameters before I get to it this afternoon.
Oh no. I'll pull it up now, are you thinking adapter contamination, or could it be a mismatch with the reference index we updated last week?

Adapter contamination is the more likely culprit given the library prep kit. Run FastQC on the raw files first and send me the per-base quality plots. I'm in my focus block until noon so don't wait. Just ping me if it's alarming.
Running FastQC now, will have the plots to you before noon. Sorry for missing this Friday - I should have flagged the QC report before the weekend.
Hey Mark, Anna thinks she left her graphing calculator at your place Sunday. Karen's not answering, probably on a run. Can you check the kitchen counter? She needs it for Westbrook tomorrow.
Ha, found it under the couch cushion actually. Classic. Karen's at Pilates til noon. I can drop it at Westbrook on my way into the office if that helps?
That works perfectly, thank you. Drop-off closes at 8:15 so before then. I owe you both.
Done ✓ - and tell Steve he still owes me a chess rematch 😄
Raymond, Tuesday's faculty seminar at 8:30 cuts directly into Anna's drop-off at Westbrook Academy. Her spring showcase is that morning and I can't make both. Any chance we push to 10?
Completely forgot about the showcase. My apologies. 10am works fine, I'll update the invite. It's just the Genomics Initiative budget rundown anyway, shouldn't run long.
Thank you. For the record, 8:30 meetings are a productivity crime against anyone with a school-age child. Consider this filed as ongoing departmental feedback.
Noted and formally recorded. See you at 10.
Hey - doing pickup at Westbrook around 3:15, want me to grab Anna too? Would save you cutting your research block short.
Yes please. Steve's in Boston until Thursday so logistics have been tighter than usual this week. She knows to look for you.
Perfect 👍 Any chance she has her soccer kit? Ellie's got practice and figured they could hang after if Anna's up for it.
She does, I packed it this morning. Text me when you're back in Thornfield and I'll come collect her by 6.
Dorothy. RNA-seq pipeline finished overnight. Cluster 7 expression pattern is all wrong, nothing like the TCGA controls. Worth delaying the Thornfield seminar slides to dig into this first?
Yes. Send me the DESeq2 output and QC report before I'm back from Westbrook drop-off - I want the volcano plots open by 8:45.
Sent. Quick flag: is fig 3B in the current draft still provisional? Might need a full redraw if cluster 7 holds up under reanalysis.
Mark it provisional, don't touch the caption. I'm not rewriting figure legends twice in one week.
